title: macOS Automator workflow on selected text stopped working in Firefox 111.0 release
body: I use a macOS Automator workflow that translates selected text. It stopped working in Firefox 111.0: invoking the service on selected text now shows an error saying the service could not be used. Expected: the selected text is supplied to the workflow, which opens a Safari popup with the translation. Screenshot of the error attached.

symptoms_visible: Invoking the Automator selected-text service from Firefox 111.0 fails with 'service could not be used'; the workflow previously opened a translation popup with the selected text.
N0.label: N0 service error reported

symptoms_visible: Reporter traversed macOS privacy settings and found no permission toggle applicable to Firefox for this service; the suggested article covers third-party Automator actions the workflow does not use; the error is unchanged.
N1_x.label: N1_x permission-regrant aftermath

symptoms_visible: Service error persists in Firefox 111; the same workflow works in other applications and worked in earlier Firefox versions.
N2.label: N2 regression established

symptoms_visible: Service error persists; the breaking change has been bisected to the graphics-context replacement commit; a second affected user reports the same failure for URL-based workflows.
N3.label: N3 regressor bisected

symptoms_visible: The provided try build (target.dmg) runs the workflow correctly for both affected users; the installed release build still shows the error.
N4.label: N4 fix verified on try build

symptoms_visible: The partial revert has landed and is riding Firefox 112 (uplifted to 112.0b6, GA 4/11); the Automator workflow works on builds containing the fix.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Treat it as a macOS permissions problem after an OS update: re-grant Firefox the relevant service permissions in System Settings.
solution.concrete_example: Have you had a recent macOS update? You may have to grant permissions (again) in System Settings — see the linked article about enabling Automator actions.

edges.comment: Real thread c2-c5: no applicable permission toggle exists; the linked article covers third-party Automator actions the workflow does not use; direction falsified.

question_patterns: Did this workflow work in earlier Firefox versions?
Does the same service work from other applications?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes — used multiple times a day, so a breakage would be noticed immediately; it worked before the 111 update and the same action still works in other apps.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Actually it fails in every application since the last macOS update, not just Firefox.

question_patterns: What does the workflow consist of — any third-party actions?
Can you share the workflow definition?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Only default actions: receive current text from any application, run a small JavaScript that builds a translate.google.com URL from the input, open the result in a Safari popup. Screenshot of the flow and a screen recording attached.

edges.comment: Real thread c4-c7: regression established (rules out the macOS-configuration theory); workflow composition shared with screenshot and video.

question_patterns: Could you run mozregression to find the last working build?
Can we get a regression range for when the service broke?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A second affected user ran mozregression: last working build 0a665be7; the bisection lands on the commit replacing the deprecated NSGraphicsContext graphicsPort with CGContext. That user also sees the same 'problem with input to the service' failure for URL-capturing workflows.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Bisection shows the workflow already failed before Firefox 111; the breaking point is a macOS point release, with no Firefox commit in the window.
Same regressing commit found, bisected from a different starting range by another volunteer.

edges.comment: Real thread c8-c10: the regression range came from the second affected user; with it the developer could finally reproduce. Composite-user simplification: both affected users fold into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Could you run this try build (target.dmg) and verify the issue is fixed?
Please test the build with the partial revert and report whether the workflow works.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It works! (Second affected user also confirms the updated build works.) The developer's analysis: the service broke because -writeSelectionToPasteboard:types: was called with only NSStringPboardType, so part of the graphics-context change needs to be reverted.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The try build still shows the same service error for both users.

edges.comment: Real thread c11-c14, c16: verification measurement on the provided build; the root-cause reading (pasteboard types) is recorded as the engineer-inferred gain on N4.

solution.intent: Land the partial revert of the graphics-context change for macOS Services, uplift to the 112 beta, and give the reporter an honest availability timeline (112 GA on 4/11; a 111 dot release is not guaranteed and ultimately not planned).
solution.concrete_example: Partially revert the graphicsPort->CGContext change for the Services path; patch approved for 112.0b6; fix rides the trains with 112 (GA 4/11), no 111 dot release planned.

edges.comment: Resolution per c12-c25: partial revert landed, uplifted to 112.0b6; GA timeline communicated when the reporter asked about release process.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the regression: Firefox 111's replacement of NSGraphicsContext graphicsPort with CGContext broke macOS Services pasteboard writing (writeSelectionToPasteboard called with only NSStringPboardType); this is a Firefox regression, not a macOS permission problem.
Must not settle on the macOS-permission direction: it is falsified in-case (no applicable toggle; same workflow works in other apps and worked in earlier Firefox).

The fix must be verified by the reporter on a provided build before landing, and the resolution must include an honest availability timeline (uplift target and GA date; no promise of a 111 dot release).
Must treat the issue as resolved only after user verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Pragmatic daily-workflow user, moderately technical: can inspect privacy settings, install a try build from a dmg, and record a screen capture; a second, slightly more technical affected user contributes the mozregression run (both folded into one simulated user).
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise and cooperative; answers exactly what is asked; pushes back with evidence when a suggestion does not apply; asks practical follow-ups about release timelines.
